bodyHtml:
MirrorProxy is making waves in the Backend ecosystem this week, gaining 9new stars. With a total of 180 stars on GitHub and 10 forks, this open-source project is rapidly becoming a go-to tool for developers worldwide.

⭐ 180Stars
📈 +9/wkGrowth
🔀 10Forks
⚠️ 1Open Issues

Key Features

  • Written in Rust for maximum performance
  • Licensed under MIT — free to use and modify
  • Official website: https://sina.dev
  • 🏷️ mirror
  • 🏷️ proxy
  • 🏷️ rust
  • 🏷️ self-hosted

Why MirrorProxy Is Trending

The Backend landscape is constantly evolving, and MirrorProxy has emerged as one of the fastest-growing projects this week. Several factors contribute to its momentum:

  1. Growing community: With 9 new stars this week alone, developer adoption is accelerating rapidly.
  2. Active maintenance: The project sees regular updates, ensuring compatibility with the latest ecosystem changes.
  3. Practical utility: All-in-one mirror acceleration,The project uses an adapter-based proxy core and already ships adapters for GitHub, Docker/OCI, Composer, npm, PyPI, Cargo, Go modules, major language repositories, developer-tool distribution services, and operating system mirrors.

If you're working in Backend, this is definitely a project worth watching — and adopting.

Quick Start

Get started with MirrorProxy in minutes:

# Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/inbjo/MirrorProxy # Navigate to project cd MirrorProxy # Check the README for detailed setup instructions

For full documentation and advanced usage, visit the official GitHub repository.

Final Thoughts

MirrorProxy is a solid addition to any developer's toolkit. With its growing community, active development, and practical design, it's well worth your time to evaluate. Star it on GitHub, try it in a side project, and see if it fits your workflow.
